summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Keenan W. Cox completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He taught at Brown (~1960–1964) and UCLA (~1969–1994), and was a fellow at NIAS (~1974–1975).
Kei Kataoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Oxford, JSPS, the University of Tokyo, and Kyushu University.

Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He worked at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and became a professor at Kokugakuin University.

Keiji Iwata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1943–1947). He later held academic appointments at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1971–1974) and Otani University (~1984–1989).

Keiji Nishitani was a Japanese philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Freiburg under Martin Heidegger. A disciple of Kitaro Nishida, he served as a professor at Kyoto University and taught at Otani University.

Keiki Yabuki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Taisho University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Shukyo University and Taisho University, and was an associate professor at the University of Tokyo.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Keikyo Nakamikado has worked as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies (attested 2015).

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham. He held academic posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Keishi Renja completed doctoral coursework (attested 2013) and served as a research student at Taisho University.

Keishin Okamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He served on the faculty at Koyasan University and was a professor at Kochi University until 1995.

Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Tohoku University. He served as dean of Buddhist studies at Rissho University, professor at Tohoku University, and president of Hosen Gakuen College.

Keith Dowman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with traditional teachers, including Kangyur Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He became a professor at Shuchiin University and served as director of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism at Taisho University.

Keizaburo Mizuno was an art historian in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He worked at the Tokyo National Museum and Tokyo University of the Arts, later directing the Niigata Prefectural Museum and Hanzomon Museum.

Kelsang Gyatso was a Buddhist scholar and teacher who studied at Sera Monastery, earning his Geshe degree. He taught at the Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977 and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Kelsey Alise Seymour is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and held a visiting predoctoral fellowship at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science.
Kemu Jin was an Indologist, linguist, and Sinologist. He held an appointment at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

Ken McLeod is a teacher and scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MSc at the University of British Columbia, studied with Tibetan masters including Kalu Rinpoche, and served as resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985–1990).
Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.
